rationale:
Evidence from iteration 3 (score 484.4, up from 372.5): the robot still leaves the line on bends rather than oscillating. Oval finishes 14 of 20 with progress 0.94. The s-bend improved to progress 0.79 with 5 of 20 finishes, but 15 runs still went off track. The slalom is unchanged at progress 0.53, ending off track in all 20 runs, with max_error around 0.064 and 1.0 line-loss events per run. steering_oscillation is moderate (0.29 to 0.39), so damping is not the limit. The kp increase from 4.0 to 5.0 and the sensor_size increase from 0.012 to 0.016 both helped, since the s-bend progress rose and the oval finish rate rose. The remaining failures are on the tight bends, where the robot reaches the 0.06 m limit before the correction catches up.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.3 to 1.15. This gives the steering more time per bend, which is hypothesis (b) from iteration 3. Oval time should rise from about 1.9 s to about 2.3 s, still under the 3 s limit. (2) kd 1.1 to 1.4. The added damping is meant to contain the overshoot that the higher kp causes on the slalom's alternating bends. Oscillation is well below the 0.5 warning level, so this is a safe step. (3) kp stays at 5.0, and geometry, ki, sensor_weights and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the speed and damping change can be read cleanly.

Expected result: fewer off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom, with slalom progress above 0.7 and s-bend completion above 0.3. Oval completion may dip slightly because of the lower speed.

Hypotheses to test: (a) if the slalom still leaves at max_error near 0.06 with speed reduced, the slalom needs wider sensor coverage (spread to about 0.04 m, spacing 0.02 m, still under the 0.025 m tape width). (b) If oval completion falls below 0.6 because of the speed drop, base_speed should return to about 1.25 with kd kept at 1.4. (c) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.5, kd is too high relative to kp and should go back to about 1.2.

Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so I can separate the speed effect from the damping effect.
